correctness.rationale: Every label i>=3 appears only once in a diameter-three tree, and label 2 can appear at most twice on opposite-side leaves. No two all-one color parts can simultaneously dominate; an independent dominating set is exactly all leaves, {U}∪B or {V}∪A. Two opposite-side label-2 anchors cannot support k singleton-anchor groups without forcing adjacent centers color 1. A t=k coloring therefore exists only when one label-2 center is a broadcast singleton and complement is an independent dominating set of center-type cardinality; constructions give t=k for exceptions and t=k+1 generally. The 4-vertex path lower bound gives t>=3 for all k<=3.

originality.rationale: The initiating Brešar-Ferme-Hu paper defines and studies the same k-domatic packing parameter; the inspected original covers paths/cycles and subdivided double stars, not the exact all-k spectrum of the non-subdivided diameter-three double-star family. Earlier ordinary packing coloring results supply only the k=1 boundary.
residual_risks: Earlier broadcast domatic all-diameter-three classification could subsume the special family under a different name.
Only ordinary double stars a,b>=1 are covered; subdivided and larger-diameter variants excluded.
Original arxiv dated 2026-10-02 is very recent, so newer dependent papers could exist.

value.rationale: The exact all-k palette spectrum identifies two exceptional class positions determined by the two pendant multiplicities. This is a natural structural family with a nontrivial phase pattern beyond generic graph bounds; it is not just an arbitrary small case.
